Specifications

The panel is installed behind the steering wheel.

Its position guarantees maximum visibility/legibility of the information for the driver in all vehicle usage conditions (day/night) without reflections, distortions or double images.

The panel is available on the Comfort version

View of assembly

- rev counter

- fuel level gauge (with reserve warning light)

- engine coolant temperature gauge (with overheating warning light)

- milometer

- multifunction display

The views of the control panel for the 1.9 JTD 16v, 2.4 JTD 20v and 2.2 petrol versions are illustrated showing both right hand drive and left hand drive versions.

The end of scale for the speedometer on the 1.9 JTD 8v version is 200 km/h or 140 MPH.

Composition:

The panel contains 4 analogue gauges:

- Electronic speedometer

- Electronic rev counter

- Fuel level (with insufficient fuel level warning light)

- Engine coolant temperature gauge (with overheating warning light)

All the indicators are moved by a stepping motor.

There is a positive three line alphanumerical display:

The top line has 14 dot matrix characters (7x5) for the display of:

- Date

- Trip computer data (processed by the control panel);

- Set-up menu with messages for settings/adjustments;

- Messages about: activation of functions / service / failure / warning;

- Radio/telephone information repetition;

The bottom two lines in segments are for displaying:

- Milometer;

- Clock;

- Outside temperature and ICE DANGER symbol

- Headlamp alignment corrector reading;

- "Return to workshop" symbol (spanner);

- Automatic transmission information (display of gear engaged and AUTO symbol);

There is a buzzer with the possibility of managing signals of different intensity for carrying out the following functions:

- Alarm/warning/danger signals

- Doors open with the vehicle moving

- Handbrake applied with vehicle moving

- Driver's/passenger seat belt not fastened

- Driver's/passenger seat belt not fastened

- Fuel reserve

- Button pressing roger beep

- Automatic transmission signalling

- Parking sensor signalling

- Engine coolant temperature

- Insufficient engine oil pressure/level

- EOBD failure

- EBD / ABS / ESP

- TPMS (puncture only)

- AIR-BAG / SBR

- Automatic transmission fluid overheating

- Electric Steering

- DPF

- Key (TEG) not recognized

The instrument panel interfaces with:

- 5 external buttons fitted on the dashboard: “C.A.F.+”, “C.A.F. –“, “Mode”, “Mode+”, “Mode–“.

- TRIP button on the right steering column switch unit lever.

A three line transreflective technology alphanumerical display is located in the centre.

1 - milometer reading

Operation

Display at key on

The information in the standard display is:

- date (on the 14 character alphanumerical line)

- clock

- milometer

- headlamp alignment corrector information

- outside temperature

- ice symbol (in the case of ice danger)

- automatic transmission readings (where present)

With the ignition in the OFF position and the front doors closed, the display shows the clock and should not be lit up.

The moment one of the front doors is opened in the key off position, the display will show:

- clock

- milometer

Set-up menu display

Access to the menu screen

The buttons for the set-up are present in the controls, pressing "MODE" activates the ambient menu.

The + and - buttons are used for navigating inside the menu.

The menu set-up functions can be selected using the "MODE" / "+" / "-" buttons which should only be activated with the vehicle stationary with the exception of the following functions: "SPEED LIMIT EXCEEDED" (selecting activation/deactivation of speed limit and selecting speed limit level).

Not all the functions can be activated during the fault message display cycles

The operation should be the sequential type as described below.

"MODE" buttons

With 1 brief press:

- if the vehicle speed is less than 4 km/h: activation of the "complete" set-up menu and shown on the display;

- if the vehicle speed is above the 4km/h parameter: activation of the "reduced" set-up menu;

- confirmation of the selected function;

- confirmation of the setting/modification and return to the main menu screen (same option).

With 1 long press and not on the release of the button:

- memorizing of the modifications confirmed with the short press and return to the standard screen (or the screen activated before the "MODE" button was pressed briefly).

"+" / "-" keys

- Selection of functions present in the set-up menu.

- Setting/adjustment of functions present in the set-up menu;

The setting of the functions (e.g. clock adjustment) takes place in increasingly shorter steps depending on the time the button is kept pressed.

Timeout

If no operation is carried out for a period of 60 seconds, the standard screen is restored (or the screen activated before the "MODE" button was pressed).

The following functions can be displayed whilst the vehicle is being driven by pressing the "MODE" button:

- Introductory words for opening the menu

- Selecting speed limit activation/deactivation

- Selecting speed limit level

- Dusk sensor sensitivity level adjustment

- Menu exit

The following functions can be displayed whilst the vehicle is stationary by pressing the "MODE" button:

- Introductory words for opening the menu

- Selecting speed limit level

- Selecting speed limit activation/deactivation

- Dusk sensor sensitivity level adjustment

- TRIP B activation / deactivation.

-- Clock adjustment

- Hour mode (12h / 24h)

- Date adjustment

- Activation/deactivation of boot release together with unlocking of all the doors

- Activation/deactivation of unlocking of front door only

- Activation/deactivation of automatic locking of doors + boot above 20 km/h

- Setting unit of measurement for distances

- Setting unit of measurement for fuel consumption

- Language setting

- Volume of buzzer for alarms/failures/warnings

- Button pressing buzzer volume (roger beep)

- Reactivation of buzzer for SBR signalling

- Service interval display (km/miles/days)

- Menu exit

Lighting dimmer

The driver can adjustment the brightness inside the passenger compartment (lighting for graphics/gauges/control panel display and climate control) by pressing the "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons. The lighting brightness cannot however be reduced to zero.

The effect of the adjustment of the brightness (after pressing the buttons) is immediately visible.

The dimming value is transmitted by the NQS via the CAN to allow the brightness value to be sent to the other Nodes.

If the side lights are deactivated, the display is 100% lit up and the brightness cannot be adjusted (dimmed). The adjustment is only possible with the exterior lights on.

The warning lights are not subject to adjustment/dimming (brightness always 100%).

If the brightness is adjusted the first line of the display shows the message "Lighting" and the brightness adjustment symbols come on/go off.

This screen remains for 5 seconds after the lst command is given after which the previous screen is displayed.

The lighting for the display during the screens relating to the signalling of faults/information (with the exception of the ICE DANGER cycle) is not subject to adjustment/diming and the brightness always remains constant at 100% in daytime conditions (side lights deactivated).

The display lighting during screens relating to other signals is, on the other hand, subject to adjustment/dimming.

The "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons remain activated to regulate the brightness of the control panel and the other vehicle components. However the message "Lighting" is not shown on the first line of the display and the brightness adjustment symbols come on/go off.

Ice danger warning signal

To warn the driver of the possible presence of ice on the road, if the outside temperature remains below 3 degrees C, the temperature reading flashes and the "snow" symbol and the "Ice danger" message are displayed in place of the clock .

At the end of the warning cycle:

- the message disappears and the screen prior to the event reappears;

- the temperature reading stops flashing;

- the "snow symbol" remains in the special area of the display (as long as T is below 6 °C).

This display only takes one after the outside temperature is recognized to be T < 3°C and is only repeated if the temperature reaches the value T > 6°C and then returns again to T < 3°C.

If the outside temperature at the key-on is T < 3° C, then the display shows the entire diagnostic cycle at the key-on (check in progress, etc. ad defined previuosly) and later on it initiates the "warning cycle" described above.

Dusk sensor

The dusk sensor sensitivity is adjusted by means of the special item in the setup menu.

This adjustment is only possible with the vehicle stationary.

It is possible, during the display, to adjust the setting of the dusk sensor from (1 to 3) shown in the control panel display using the "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons.

Once the setting is adjusted, it is memorized in the control panel and transmited on the CAN.

The last setting memorized is displayed when the dedicated item is selected.

The set-up menu item that allows the adjustment of the sensitivity levels is also present when the dusk sensor is present but not activated.

This item should only appear if the dusk sensor is not present.

Clock display

The reading in hh:mm should always remain present at the key on and at the key off.

The clock adjustment is an item in the set-up menu.

It is also possible to select the hh:mm information from the set-up menu in 24h mode (0 - 23 h) or in 12h mode (1 - 12) without the indications AM and PM.

Outside temperature reading

The outside temperature reading should be guaranteed in standard screen conditions.

At the key on, until the NQS receives the first frame with the outside temperature information, the part of the display dedicted to this information will show nothing; if, as a result of problems with the signal, the outside temperature information continues not to be present in the network for longer than the standard recovery time, some dashes with the unit of measurement set will be displayed in place of the temperature, e.g.: (---°C).

Planned maintenance

When the planned maintenance (so-called service) is close to the next interval, this is displayed automatically at the key on (after the initial check procedure), the spanner symbol and the "service" message followed by the number of kilometres or miles (depending on the unit of measurement set using the set-up menu (see chapter on "Functions that can be selected/activated using the "MODE"/"+"/"-") buttons until the next service.

The display of the programmed maintenance information can also be shown if the user requests by selecting a special item in the setup menu.

In this case the display is possible, irrespective of the intervals.

The starting figure of 30,000 km is then suitably converted into miles by the control panel, in order to guarantee that the levels are recognized, corresponding to the signals in the display (as defined in the next paragraph).

Counter reset by the service network

At each service interval, the Service personnel should:

- reset the "km" (or miles) counter to the starting vlue (30,000 km/18,000 mi) using the diagnostic equipment. It should be possible to read/rewrite the data using the diagnostic equipment.

- memorize that the Planned Maintenance (service) has taken place. There should be a trace of the last service carried out, through the indication: service date/ service no. carriedout / total mileage. It should be possible to read/rewrite the data using the diagnostic equipment. The number of the service should decrease at each Reset-Info-Service beginning with the starting figure = 9 (decreasing from 9 to 0).

If the instrument panel is being replaced, the Service personnel should:

- reset the km/mi in the milometer.

- read the number of services carried out and enter them into the new panel.

- read the km/mi counters until the next service and enter them into the new panel.

- read the last service date and rewrite it in the new control panel.

If the battery is disconnected the data memorized in the control panel will be preserved.

The only settings that need resetting are the date and the time.

Follow me home function

The following are shown on the control panel display:

- the "follow me home" function activated message.

- The total seconds set using the steering column switch unit which should not decrease during the display.

- After the steering column switch unit has been pressed 7 times (210 seconds) it cannot increase further.

The display of the screen for the FOLLOW ME HOME function remains for 20 seconds starting from the last time the steering column switch unit is pressed unless the function is deactivated during the display using the left steering column switch unit lever.

This also takes place after the steering column switch unit is pressed for the seventh time.

Rev counter

This indicates the engine rpm with the help of a stepping motor.

The control electronics and the operation is achieved by means of a microprocessor which guarantees the precision of the signal in the gauge.

Odometer

When starting, the milometer display shows the total or trip mileage in km memorized at the previous key off.

The tripmeter is reset by keeping the TRIP button in the steering column switch unit pressed for more than 2 secs.; the total mileage can also be zeroed only once within the first 200 km.

In the case of a new instrument the mileage reading is preceeded by and "H", after the first 200 km the letter "H" disappears automatically.

Fuel level gauge

The reading is the analogue type produced by a stepping motor, the control electronics and operation is achieved using a microprocessor.

The fuel level is measured by a sensor in the tank which informs the Body Computer by means of an interface (microprocessor) transforming it into a percentage value.

The system guarantees that there are no fluctuations/errors in the readings for the fuel gauge.

The reading for the fuel reserve is siganlled by both the warning light and an acoustic signal through a buzzer inside the panel.

Engine coolant temperature gauge

The reading is the analogue type produced by a stepping motor, the control electronics and operation is achieved through a microprocessor, the red sector in the gaug signals the max. temperature correspondingn to the danger zone.

The display cycle can be interrupted in two ways:

- removing the cause of the malfunction that produced the problem;

- the driver pressing the "MODE" button. In this case the screen prior to the fault will be reproposed but the signal should be kept activted through the warning light in the panel which should remain on until the cause of the malfunction that produced the fault is solved.

The message corresponding to the TRIP function activated should be shown on the display (in other words in addition to "B" for selecting Trip B). It should be possible to exclude the display for TRIP B from the set-up menu. The control panel should always process the data for Trip B and then transmit it via the CAN even when the display in the actual panel is excluded using the set-up menu.

Recovery

If information is missing (no relevant CAN signals) some of the TRIP data will display the message "not available".

If the speed sensor is faulty, all the TRIP counters display dashes "----" together with the data characteristics (with units of measurement) for each item (km or mi for range , km/h or mph for average speed etc.).

If the fuel level sensor is faulty, dashes only "----" will be displayed for the Range, together with descriptions (with the relevant units of measurement) for each item.

If the instant fuel consumption signal is not validated, dashes "-----" will be displayed for the Range, Average consumption, Instantaneous consumption together with descriptions (with the relevant unit of measurement) for each item.

If the malfunction disappears, the counting of the various items continues in their different ways and the values downloaded prior to the mission are not reset and the mission is not restarted.

Range

The range indicates the estimated distance (in km or miles) that the car could travel with the fuel currently in the tank, assuming the mission is continued applying the same driving style (same fuel consumption conditions).

The range is calculated using the following information:

- received from the NBC;

- instantaneous mileage;

- fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank);

- received from the NCM; instantaneous fuel consumption (in litres/hour);

- fuel tank capacity, in litres (calibration parameter entered during the EOL programming - supplier).

when the range is calculated for versions with DPR (Diesel Particulate Filter) a different value is used for the calculation parameters.

Distance travelled

The distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission is indicated, i.e. from when the user carried out a rest by pressing the dedicated button.

The reading is consistent with the display on the total mileage recorder.

Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each new mission (reset), the display shows "0:0", after which the calculated value is displayed.

At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed.

When the maximum possible distance is reached, the mileage display should be automatically zeroed and, at the same time, there is a total TRIP reset with the exception of the Range and Instantaneous Consumption items.

The calculation of the Distance Travelled is activated at the key on.

The distance reading should be displayed and sent on the CAN with:

- range between 0 and 9999.9 km (or mi)

- resolution of 0.1 km (or miles)

- update of display: every 0.1 km (or miles)

Average fuel consumption

Average fuel consumption measn the ratio between distance travelled since the start of the mission and number of litres consumed since the start of the mission.

The control panel downloads the fuel consumption signal via the CAN and processes it to divide it by the distance travelled since the start of the mission.

The calculation is only carried out with the engine running (300 rpm).

At the start of a new mission, due to the battery being reconnected, the average consumption figure is initialized at the "predefined average standard consumption" value personalized for the vehicle/engine type. At the start of a new mission due, on the other hand, to a reset (by the user by pressing the dedicated button or a reset of one of the TRIP parameters) the Average Consumption value is initialized at the "average consumption value calculated during the previous mission". A weighting to be attributed to the above initial value to avoid excessive fluctuations in the reading shown during the first few minutes of the mission. The information displayed tends to represent the actual mission consumption condition within 3 minutes and the effect of the standard data becomes nil within 3 minutes.

The value displayed is equal to "----" for a distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission equal to the parameter 500 m, after which the value calculated will be displayed.

At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed.

The displayed average consumption is equal to"----", whenever:

- The user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button.

- One of the TRIP parameters is reset.

The value is displayed and sent on the CAN with:

- resolution of 0.1 km/l (or mpg)

- calculation precision: < 0.1 km/l (or mpg)

- display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s

- max value shown equal to 50 km/litre - 2 l/100km -99.9 mpg

- min value shown equal to 4 km/litre - 25 l/100km - 2mpg

Instantaneous fuel consumption

The Instantaneous Fuel Consumption refers to the value of litres of fuel consumed per unit of distance travelled by the vehicle during the mission.

The value displayed makes the user aware of the differences in fuel consumption connected with the style of driving without varying excessively and/or with inconsistent values.

The Instantaneous Fuel Consumption is calculated using the following information:

- received from the NBC; - instantaneous mileage

- received from the NCM; instantaneous fuel consumption (in litres/hour)

Average speed

The average speed is calculated from the beginning of the mission, as a ratio between distance travelled and trip time.

The calculation is only carried out with the engine running (300 rpm).

Each time the battery is connected and at the start of each new mission (reset) the display will show "----" for a distance travelled by the vehicle from the start of the mission equal to the parameter 500 m after which the value calculated will be displayed.

At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed.

The displayed average speed is equal to"----", whenever:

- The user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button.

- One of the TRIP parameters is reset.

The value is displayed and sent on the CAN with:

- resolution of 0.1 km/h (or miles)

- calculation precision: < 0.1 km/h

- display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s (10 s ± 0.1 s ).

Journey time

The trip time shows the time elapsed from the start of the mission, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the dedicated button or an automatic reset occurred

Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each new mission (reset), the display shows "0:00", after which the calculated value is displayed.

At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is displayed.

If the vehicle is parked with the engine off (key off), the accumulated trip counter stops but does not reset to zero. The count resumes as soon as the vehicle sets off again (next key on - engine running).

The counting of the Journey Time is activated at the key on with the engine running (parameter 300 rpm).

Starting at the key on, the Journey Time is indicated in hh:mm and is sent on the CAN with:

- range between 0:00 and 99:59

- resolution equal to 1 min.

- display updated every minute

- data update every second

- the two dots between hh and mm flash during normal operation (frequency 1 Hz. – D.C. 50%)

When the maximum possible value is reached (99.59), the journey time display should be automatically zeroed and, at the same time, there is a total TRIP reset with the exception of the Range and Instantaneous Consumption items.

Buzzer specifications

The buzzer function is produced by a piezoelectric acoustic signal. On versions with auto. trans. the buzzer is also responsible for the signals coming from the CAN as well as the specific signals for the Automatic Transmission. The function is also activated with the key off.

Buzzer function access priority

Since the buzzer function on the automatic transmission version is shared between the requirements of the panel and the requirements of the automatic transmission control unit, access priority is given to the Automatic Transmission Node function. This Node notifies the Panel of the decision/desire to activate the buzzer; the signal is the low active type and is managed directly by the microprocesssor. If the Automatic Transmission Node activation signal is present , the buzzer is activated by the electronic structure inside the Panel. In the case of a short circuit to earth for the pin involved, the stage is protected by there will be an increase in the stand by current.

DPF SYSTEM

On vehicles equipped with this system (DPF) certain operating conditions may occur on diesel engines that will have the following impact on the customer:

1) Particle Filter blocked: the GENERAL FAILURE warning light is activated and/or the display of a specific message in the Control Panel display (QdB) combined with an acoustic signal

2)Engine oil in poor condition: the minimum engine oil pressure warning light flashes with a specific message in the Control Panel display.

Warnings to the customer

If the Particle Filter is blocked, the following message is displayed: "Pollution control filter blocked, see manual" plus an acoustic signal

If the oil is in poor condition, the minimum oil pressure warning light will flash and the display will show the following message: "Change the engine oil".

The warning light must be reset at each oil change.
